text:
jane_support: Hey team, Acme reported a sustained drop in embeddings throughput since ~02:00 UTC. Tokens/sec looks steady but vectors/sec is ~60% lower. Customer says request payloads unchanged. attaching a short sample and their request id: req_0x9a7c

mike_runtime: thanks. can you paste one full request/response (sanitized) + the request id you saw in logs? is this affecting all models or just their chosen embeddings model?

jane_support: pasted below (sanitized). model: text-embed-3-small, req id: req_0x9a7c, region: us-west-2. note: spikes in queue depth around 02:05-02:20.

---begin---
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-3-small","input":["doc1","doc2",...]}'

Response headers: X-Redwood-Req: req_0x9a7c, X-Vec-Dim: 384
Response latency: 120ms (token path), vectors/sec: ~48 (was ~120 at 01:30)
---end---

raj_sre: can you also share the customer concurrency (# of parallel clients) and typical batch sizes? queue backlog sounds like backpressure at GPU slots.

jane_support: Acme says client concurrency steady at 8 and batch sizes mostly 16. they said nothing changed on their side.

deploy-bot: Rollout event: routing-service v2.9.1 -> v2.10.0 started at 01:58 UTC, gradual 100% by 02:10 UTC.

mike_runtime: aha — routing rollout timed with the onset. v2.10 changed batch-window default from 20ms -> 40ms for latency smoothing. that can increase effective batch sizes and push GPU queue depth. still, that usually improves vectors/sec. puzzling.

raj_sre: let's look at GPU metrics. from the affected pool (us-west-2, pool-id gpupool-7) I see average GPU utilization unchanged, but pending queue length jumped 2.5x and kv-cache hits dropped. could be misrouted smaller-dim shards packing suboptimally.

mike_runtime: can you run a repro that simulates Acme traffic? simple script to hammer embeddings at batch size 16 concurrency 8 for 5m. include header X-Redwood-Test: acme-sim.

raj_sre: running now. quick logs:

```
[02:06:12] sent 128 requests/s (batch16 x8)
[02:06:20] observed queue_depth=18 -> 46
[02:07:00] vectors/sec per GPU dropped from 3600 -> 1100
[02:07:40] rate limiter kicks in, 429s ~0.3%
```

raj_sre: also noting many requests had `x-vec-dim: 384` header but some internal worker logged `expected_dim=512` — mismatch on model variant mapping.

mike_runtime: that mapping discrepancy is key. rolling change in routing-service added a fallback path for variant-models but we missed mapping for text-embed-3-small v2 (512) -> v1 (384). when variant mismatch occurs, system falls back to CPU quantized executor causing throughput collapse.

jane_support: ok, customer is on text-embed-3-small v1 (384). can we force routing to prefer v1 for their account while we patch?

mike_runtime: yes. temporary mitigation: set route override for tenant acme_corp -> model=text-embed-3-small:v1 in routing console or via API. that will route them to GPU-backed pool with proper kernel selection.

beth_billing: FYI customer faced billing spikes due to retries. if we patch, should we issue credit for the 02:00-03:00 window? they hit ~2.5x token/vec cost because of retries.

jane_support: Emily (customer) responded in DMs, wants repro steps for us to run while they remain on cutoff window.

emily_acme_cust: thanks for the quick triage. please keep me posted. happy to accept a temporary override. we can pause traffic if you need a hotfix deploy.

mike_runtime: plan: 1) apply route override for acme_corp -> text-embed-3-small:v1 (immediate). 2) revert the routing-service default mapping change in next patch (minor config). 3) run controlled test and confirm vectors/sec recovers. 4) evaluate credits with billing.

raj_sre: applied override at 02:18 UTC. running the same sim now.

raj_sre: quick post-override logs:
```
[02:19:05] queue_depth stabilizes at 12
[02:19:40] vectors/sec per GPU back to ~3500
[02:20:00] 429s -> 0
```

mike_runtime: looks good. root cause: routing variant fallback + mapping gap caused CPU fallback for some shards. fix will be a mapping table update + add a unit test to guard model-dim mapping.

beth_billing: will draft credit note for 02:00-02:20 window. also flagging to CS to send customer note.

jane_support: thanks everyone. i'll update the customer thread and close the escalation after billing note. :thumbsup:

emily_acme_cust: confirmed throughput recovered, thanks for the quick fix! :relieved:
